entries.title: White Sox season ends with 2-0 shutout loss to Guardians in decisive ALDS Game 5
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND – Ultimately, at the end of the Guardians’ 2-0 Game 5 victory to clinch the American League Division Series over the White Sox on Saturday night at Progressive Field, it can be safely said that right-hander Gavin Williams didn’t seem tired after throwing 18 pitches two nights prior at Rate Field.</p><p>After the White Sox offense–the most productive in the AL all year–frustrated Williams his five previous starts against them in 2026, the towering right-hander dominated the South Siders in a signature performance Saturday night at Progressive Field. Williams, the AL strikeout leader this season, broke the Guardians franchise single-game postseason record for strikeouts by blowing 98 mph by Brenton Doyle for his 12th punchout, and the first out of the sixth.</p><p>For the sixth-straight time this year, the Sox kept Williams from completing six innings against them, rallying to load the bases with two outs in the sixth. But since left-hander Erik Sabrowski blew away Munetaka Murakami to strand three runners–as Randal Grichuk waited in the on-deck circle for a run-scoring opportunity against a lefty that never arrived–that seems well besides the point. In covering the final five outs, Guardians closer Cade Smith held up all right too, despite pitching in every game of this series.</p><p>Certainly, it doesn’t seem like Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez’s left wrist is bothering him anymore, after a season where he struggled for months to recover from a fractured hamate bone. Perhaps, it’s better said that it’s simply not stopping him. Capping off a monster final three games of the ALDS, and in the wake of homering off a triple-digit, letter-high Jordan Hicks heater for a go-ahead run in Game 4, Ramirez ripped an ankle-high Sean Burke curveball over the right-field fence to put the Guardians up for good in the fourth.</p><p>Where Ramirez’s diminished state looked to be the reason the Guardians lacked for answers while dropping the first two games of the series, he drove in seven runs over the final three to send his club–the perennial division contender the White Sox dream of one day being–to their second ALCS in the last four years. Few teams have a true franchise player as reliable as Ramirez, and the Sox are not yet one of them.</p><p>Finally, even with the teams sitting at nine wins apiece across their regular and postseason matchups, it seems like the Guardians can clearly say they’re better than this year’s White Sox. The margins in the regular season standings, in the head-to-head season series, and in this ALDS all were razor thin to the point of genuine comedy.</p><p>“We had a moment after Game 4 where we ran into each other in the hallway and kind of shared like, of course, we're going to play five games,” said Guardians manager Stephen Vogt of Sox manager Will Venable. “I have so much respect for what he and that group have done over there. And we've just laughed all year because we play one-run games. The whole series was defined by one run.”</p><p>But the Guardians, in a three-game series at their home park in September, staring down elimination in front of raucous crowds at Rate Field desperate to see their club’s first postseason series victory clinched in Chicago since 1906, beat the White Sox when it mattered. They won the decisive games that delivered them another division banner to raise, they won the decisive game that granted them a chance to play for the AL title.</p><p>And in the finale, a young White Sox team that played over their heads all year were left not just with a sense that their time has yet to arrive, but that there are flaws to address if they want to go farther next October, which go beyond simply needing more starting pitchers.</p><p>The Sox offense mashed this year, but their 211 home runs came with the trade-off of the fifth-highest strikeout rate in baseball. With their season on the line in Cleveland, they struck out an MLB nine-inning postseason record 21 times. The notion of pinch-hitting for Murakami with the bases loaded and two outs in the sixth made statistical sense–the Sox first baseman hit .180/.349/.376 against southpaws in the regular season, while Grichuk led the league in slugging against them–but also would cut at the very identity of this 2026 club.</p><p>That said, the centerpiece of this team, the Japanese sluggers whose arrival signaled to the White Sox clubhouse that the organization was serious about contention this season, had the lowest contact rate in MLB among qualified hitters. Colson Montgomery had the second-lowest. These are warts that were exposed as the offense that launched the White Sox into October, could not do enough to capture the ALDS against an elite Guardians pitching staff.</p><p>It’s a cruel ending for a White Sox team that should largely be remembered for bringing joy back to the ballyard on the South Side of Chicago, that played together in a way that allowed them to transcend raw ingredients that had no one projecting them to reach this far. But the reward for good seasons are usually cruel endings. The bitter taste of defeat is meant to linger until champagne can replace it.</p><p>“The perception of us and this organization has enhanced that for us, in which we're even more motivated to prove everyone wrong and to change the perception of what the White Sox are,” said Venable. “We have a bunch of guys that are committed to that.”</p><p>The commitment must remain, but another opportunity to prove it must wait until next year.</p>

entries.title: Blackhawks' weaknesses exposed by Hurricanes' pressure in predictable loss
entries.summary: <p>Given how much the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> have struggled to cleanly exit their defensive zone this season, the defending champion Hurricanes seemed like they would pose a particularly brutal matchup Saturday.</p><p>That's exactly how things played out in a 5-2 Hawks loss.</p><p>Every time a young Hawks defenseman circled deep into his zone to retrieve a puck, he was swarmed instantly by Hurricanes forecheckers, who have mastered their signature man-on-man system. And when the Hawks did get some space to move the puck, those passes didn't find teammates frequently enough.</p><p>With Connor Bedard recovering from surgery and Frank Nazar serving the first half of his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/10/09/blackhawks-frank-nazar-suspended-islanders-bo-horvat" >two-game suspension</a>, there's no doubt the Hawks' forward corps are handicapped. But they aren't providing enough puck support for the defensemen, either.</p><p>"There are times, especially [facing] this team, where you have to live to fight another day," defenseman Alex Vlasic said. "[You] check your shoulder and if the rim is there, use it. But if it’s not — which, a lot of times, it’s not — you’re going to have to maybe absorb the hit and just chip it into space, get it out of the zone. </p><p>"We didn’t do that as well as we probably could have, and they just kept it in our zone and kept tiring us out [by] cycling it low-to-high."</p><p>The Hurricanes broke the game open with three goals in less than five minutes of game time straddling the first intermission. </p><p>The first goal exposed another instance where the Hawks lost their "F3" (high forward) and conceded a transition attack. The second exposed the Hawks' mightily struggling power play — and an untimely broken stick for Bowen Byram. The third exposed another Hawks weakness: defensive sorting.</p><p>"We’re not mirroring [the Hurricanes'] systems, but in terms of pressure and things like that, that’s how we want to play," Hawks coach Jeff Blashill said. "So it’s a good lesson for our guys."</p><p>Roman Kantserov's first career NHL goal provided very short-lived happiness to a United Center crowd of 18,120 — a somewhat disappointing number for the first weekend home game of the season.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">GOAL: Roman Kantserov scores his FIRST NHL GOAL on a breakaway! <a href="https://t.co/XspQsbWnu1">pic.twitter.com/XspQsbWnu1</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2109075637126455377?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Hawks are now 1-5-0 with a minus-14 goal differential after two weeks of regular-season action during which not much has gone right. They desperately need to change their trajectory next week as they enter the thick of this seven-game home stand.</p><p>Blashill admitted, after Patrick Kane did the same, that some frustration is gradually seeping into the Hawks' locker room. But he followed that comment up with an emphatic statement of long-term belief.</p><p>"This group is going to win," Blashill said. "I can’t tell you if we’re going to start winning Tuesday, next week, a year from now. I have no idea when it’s going to be. But this group’s going to win, 100%."</p><h3><b>Nazar’s view</b></h3><p>On Saturday morning, Nazar shared his viewpoint on his Thursday hit on Islanders forward Bo Horvat that prompted the NHL discipline.</p><p>"They block a shot, and I just see the Islanders player going to make an attempt for the empty net," Nazar said. "[I was] on the other side of him, so the best I can do is try to apply pressure so he doesn't score. I kept my shoulders in, kept my elbow in, didn't lunge or reach or anything. Just skated right through."</p><p>Nazar added that he was still "going over everything" regarding the suspension and that he had texted Horvat to check in; Horvat responded that he was doing well.</p><p>"I don't want to let my team down and not be able to play, so that part sucks," Nazar said.</p><p>Teuvo Teravainen recovered faster than expected from his lower-body injury and was able to play Saturday, so the Hawks avoided having to call up another forward to replace Nazar.</p><h3><b>Olczyk returns</b></h3><p>Beloved former Hawks player and broadcaster Eddie Olczyk has returned to the organization after four seasons with the Kraken, the Hawks announced Saturday.</p><p>Olczyk will serve as a team ambassador — joining Denis Savard, Chris Chelios, Jeremy Roenick and Pat Foley in that role — and as a studio analyst on select Chicago Sports Network broadcasts, particularly on Saturdays.</p><p>He still works as a broadcaster for TNT, whose main NHL package airs on Wednesdays.</p><p>"To come home and represent the Blackhawks as an ambassador means more to me than I can put into words," Olczyk said in a statement. "Chicago is my home, the Blackhawks are my team, and my family and I are thrilled to be back with our fans."</p>

entries.title: Sean Burke gives White Sox what they've been missing — and need more of
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — The White Sox needed a regular baseball game Saturday night. They needed a starting pitcher to do what a starting pitcher is supposed to do: stay in the game longer than a few innings. They didn’t need an opener, a made-up role that precedes the starting pitcher, who then becomes what’s known as a “bulk” reliever.</p><p>The Sox have used both all season, bastardizing the record books and making it so anyone can pitch at any time in a game. It offends baseball purists and throws the natural order of the game out of whack.</p><p>But after a regular season full of pitching oddities and six postseason games of chaos, the Sox tasked right-hander Sean Burke, their best starting pitcher in the regular season, to be that again in Game 5 of the American League Division Series against the Guardians.</p><p>And he delivered from the start, throwing three perfect innings with two strikeouts. Maybe the Sox finally would have that elusive regular baseball game and the bullpen phone could get a well-deserved break.</p><p>In the fourth, though, Burke ran into trouble. After Steven Kwan’s leadoff single, Jose Ramirez continued his torrid stretch with a two-run homer just over the wall in right field. The ball traveled only 348 feet and, according to Statcast, wouldn’t have been a homer in 20 of 30 ballparks. But this ballpark is the only one that mattered.</p><p>Worse yet, the pitch wasn’t even a mistake. Burke threw a knuckle curveball that Ramirez golfed out of the park. It was so low, it had no business being hit. Ramirez’s other home run in the series came on a 99.9 mph fastball from Jordan Hicks that was above the strike zone. When you’re hot, you’re hot.</p><p>It was the Guardians’ only damage against Burke, who lasted five innings — not ideal for a starter, but certainly better than the Sox have gotten consistently from their staff this season. Sox general manager Chris Getz knows that the way the team has been deploying its pitchers has been suboptimal.</p><p>“We weren’t trying to create the wheel; we were trying to optimize the group that we had,” Getz said during the Sox’ celebration in Houston last week. “So much of our game is reliant on starting pitching. We would’ve liked to do that, but if we were trying to win games, we had to lean on the strengths of the club, and we’ve done that.”</p><p>Indeed they have, though it has put them in a more and more precarious position with each passing playoff game. The pitching staff has been huffing and puffing, but the only house getting blown in lately has been the Sox’ house. They used seven pitches in consecutive losses at Rate Field, sending the series back to Progressive Field.</p><p>Of course, the Guardians have been in the same boat, showing how poor the AL has been this season. After the effort it took both teams to get through four games of the series, the Rays figured to have a clear path through the AL Championship Series no matter who advanced.</p><p>Which goes back to what Getz said about baseball being reliant on starting pitching. Sox fans fondly remember the 2005 World Series champions, who had had four pitchers — Mark Buehrle, Jon Garland, Jose Contreras and Freddy Garcia — make at least 32 starts, and each threw a complete game in the ALCS victory against the Angels.</p><p>That never would happen today, but that doesn’t mean starting pitching is any less important. It sounds old-school, but teams still need at least three starters to navigate the postseason. The Sox have had one, Burke, and he didn’t even start in the division series until Game 5. He threw 5 ⅓ innings of relief in Game 2, the longest a Sox pitcher has lasted this postseason.</p><p>“Obviously, we’ve been creative and have done different things to do whatever it takes to find the path to victory,” manager Will Venable said during the series. “The things that we’re doing have been done before and been done a lot.</p><p>“I don't think that we're necessarily doing anything innovative. I think whether it’s in the regular season or in the playoffs, teams do what they have to do to figure things out. Some teams use traditional starters and have guys going seven innings. Some teams are mixing and matching and doing different things.</p><p>Like Getz, Venable knows the Sox’ success with “mixing and matching” won’t change how the team or major-league baseball views starting pitching. It’s still a necessity. Yes, postseason baseball is different, but starting pitching is the same no matter what time of year it is.</p>

entries.title: Packers to honor former Bears coach Mike Ditka with moment of silence before game Sunday at Lambeau Field
entries.summary: <p>The Packers will honor former <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Mike Ditka, one of their all-time rivals, with a moment of silence Sunday before their game against the Bears at Lambeau Field, a Green Bay spokesperson said.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/1985-bears-championship-team-remembers-former-coach-mike-ditka-as-tip-of-the-spear" >Ditka died Friday at 86</a>, and while he was a vocal antagonist who went 15-5 against the Packers as head coach, they issued a statement calling him an essential figure in the rivalry.</p><p>“One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football,” it said. “He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports.</p><p>“While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers.”</p><p>The Packers also held a moment of silence in 1999 when the Bears visited shortly after Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton died.</p>

entries.title: Woman, 22, dies after shot in Little Village
entries.summary: <p>A 22-year-old woman was fatally wounded after she was shot Saturday night in Little Village, Chicago police said. </p><p>The unidentified woman was standing on a street along the 2800 block of West 23rd Street around 8:43 p.m. when she reported hearing a loud noise and later feeling pain, police said. </p><p>She was transported by ambulance to Mount Sinai Hospital and was listed in critical condition with a gunshot wound to the armpit before later dying, police said. </p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating.<br></p>

entries.title: On Blackhawks' penalty kill, Anton Frondell, Frank Nazar handling surprisingly big roles
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> coach Jeff Blashill decided to stick with his unique penalty-killing system this season despite significant turnover in personnel.</p><p>The system is a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/01/14/blackhawks-penalty-kill-nhl-system-change-jeff-blashill-connor-murphy" >hybrid</a> between the standard "diamond" and "push-down" types and worked brilliantly last season, when the Hawks finished second in the NHL in penalty-killing rate (83.6%).</p><p>Blashill expected it would take time for the new killers to acclimate, like it has in the past. Indeed, the Hawks have allowed five power-play goals against in their first six games — while scoring just one power-play goal themselves.</p><p>The power play's ineptitude is seriously concerning. It ranks last in scoring chances per minute by a large margin. </p><p>But the penalty kill's under-the-hood numbers actually aren't bad. It has allowed the 11th-fewest chances per minute while generating the third-most shorthanded chances per minute.</p><p>"We're doing a good job of being able to contain the rush, the break-ins," Jordan Greenway said Saturday. "Maybe in-zone, we can find ways to do the job a little bit better."</p><p>Defensive defensemen Alex Vlasic and Ian Cole lead the Hawks in shorthanded ice time, and all three members of the team's most defense-oriented forward line — Greenway, Cole Smith and Ryan Greene — are taking regular shifts.</p><p>But it's interesting that young, talented centers Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar are right up there with Smith, Greene and Greenway in penalty-killing ice time.</p><p>It's particularly surprising in Frondell's case, since rookie forwards are rarely trusted in such high-pressure defensive situations and Frondell rarely killed last season in Sweden.</p><p>Blashill was willing to go out on a limb to make Frondell a center, though, and he's willing to do the same with this assignment.</p><p>"Frondell hasn't killed a lot, but I think he's got the skill set to be a very good killer," Blashill said. "And he's doing a good job. He's really, really strong on his stick. He really wins a ton of stick battles, which is a huge thing.</p><p>"He's smart in terms of making the reads and having good instincts within the system, and...he'll get better and better at winning faceoffs."</p><p>Frondell isn't about to turn down any assignments.</p><p>"[I] go in, try to win the battle, win the puck, block shots and get it out of the zone," Frondell said. "It's an easy way to create energy for the team. And I want to be on the ice as much as possible, so...I'm trying to learn it so I can play."</p><p>A substantial amount of learning is necessary. Not only is Hawks' penalty-killing system somewhat complicated by NHL standards, but also the general Swedish philosophy differs from the NHL philosophy.</p><p>"Here, it feels like it's a lot more aggressive, so much more pressure," he said. "You want to stay close [to your man]. If one guy goes, the other three should be ready to go and jump on a guy. In Sweden, it was more [about] holding your position, taking away passing lanes."</p><p>Nazar, meanwhile, had taken on a bigger penalty-killing role this season prior to his two-game suspension. His shorthanded ice time has leapt from 1:07 to 1:39 per game.</p><p>Blashill talked to Nazar over the summer about being stronger in puck battles and scrappier getting to loose pucks, and he has improved in those areas.</p><p>Blashill noted Nazar still needs to improve at grinding through long shifts on the kill. When he gets tired, he sometimes becomes too stationary; he needs to keep his feet moving. </p><p>But when he's fresh, his speed makes him a dangerous weapon when there's extra ice available. He has already generated two shorthanded breakaways this season, although both were saved.</p><p>"You're going up against arguably that team's best offensive players, so not all the best offensive players are the best defensively," Nazar said. "There's always room for opportunity there."</p>

entries.title: Rivalry resumes: What to watch for in Bears-Packers when each team has the ball
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down what to expect Monday night when <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> visit the Packers:</p><p><b>WHEN THE BEARS HAVE THE BALL</b></p><p>It’s time for wide receiver Rome Odunze to stamp his name on the Bears-Packers rivalry. DJ Moore put up big numbers against them over the last two seasons, but he’s gone and there’s a production void to fill. Tight end Colston Loveland dominated in the playoff win last season, and the Bears need Odunze to join the party, too.</p><p>Odunze has played in just three of a possible five games against the Packers in his career, including playoffs, and has totaled 10 catches for 127 yards and no touchdowns.</p><p>He might be finding his groove, however. After just eight catches over the first three games, he broke out with six for 94 against the Jets. That included a 37-yard reception from Tyson Bagent to convert a third down, and that’s the type of impact the Bears envisioned him making when they drafted him ninth overall.</p><p>With a backup quarterback stepping in, the surest options in the passing game should emerge as the most targeted.</p><p>Loveland is an obvious choice because of his size and catch radius. Odunze should be right there with him because he’s one of the Bears’ larger receivers and is ultra-reliable in route-running precision. Bears coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/09/01/the-bears-and-their-fans-needed-a-truth-teller-they-got-one-in-new-coach-ben-johnson" >Ben Johnson</a> once called him starter Caleb Williams’ “blankie” because he was always available when the pocket broke down.</p><p>This is a pivotal season for Odunze, who, like Williams, is playing for a contract extension at the end of the season. After a slow start, he’s in position to stack up a convincing argument.</p><p><b>WHEN THE PACKERS HAVE THE BALL</b></p><p>The Bears’ defensive line has a prime opportunity to assert itself and against a battered Green Bay offensive line. With injuries to starting guards Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk, the Packers signed 36-year-old Kevin Zeitler, who might start Sunday.</p><p>Pro Football Focus ranked this o-line last in the NFL, and the broad statistics back that up. The Packers are averaging a league-low 58 yards rushing per game, which puts them on track for one of the worst seasons in history, and have allowed pressure on 24.1% of their pass plays, which is 10th-highest. That instability can undercut everything for an offense.</p><p>Whether the Bears can do enough up front to exploit that is another matter. Defensive line has been a sore spot for them for years, but everything about their defense has been trending up since the start of the season.</p><p>Since allowing 37 points to the Panthers in the opener, the Bears have held opponents to 28 total. In those three games against the Vikings, Eagles and Jets, they allowed just 95 yards rushing per game.</p><p>They also rank third in the NFL in pressure rate, putting heat on the opposing quarterback on 35.3% of pass plays, but haven’t converted those into sacks.</p><p>For the Bears to take advantage on the line of scrimmage, they badly need big games from defensive end Montez Sweat and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett. They have almost 15% of their salary-cap space allotted to those two players, and Sweat has two sacks and Jarrett has none. Those two must lead the way.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Happier alone, woman still hasn't divorced
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My mom and my wonderful canine companion passed away within six months. My husband has battled addiction for years. I discovered the extent of it after I had two small children and was ending our marriage. He went to AA, sobered up and was wonderful for the next 10 years. During that time, we had two more children.</p><p>We sacrificed enormously to give them everything, including college educations. Now my children rarely speak to me, and one won't speak to me at all because of politics. My spouse has returned to his addiction. Grief over losing my two best friends has overwhelmed me. Although I am terribly lonely, I suffer terrible social anxiety due to a traumatic incident in my teens.</p><p>Six months ago, I moved into my mother's home, which is jointly owned by surviving siblings. I love being alone. I keep myself busy, and I am enjoying the most peace I have ever had in my life. I have been diagnosed with PTSD and have had years of therapy. I don't work. My spouse gives me an allowance, but living apart has resulted in my being in debt.</p><p>I just want to be left alone, but my spouse controls the purse strings. He doesn't mind the separation because it allows him to continue his addiction. Everything I pursued in my life — marriage, career, family — has amounted to nothing. At 62, I'm tired of trying. I take medicine. My internist knows of the trauma I suffered and is good at staying on top of my mental health. Is my desire to be alone with my pets and limited social interaction OK? — <i>UNSETTLED IN TEXAS</i></p><p><b>DEAR UNSETTLED:</b> You state that you and your husband are separated, and that he controls the purse strings. It's time to talk with a family law attorney about what your financial picture would look like if you were to divorce. I wouldn't want to live alone at 62, but if that's the lifestyle you prefer, I won't judge.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My wife's family holds gatherings several times a year for various holidays. I'm always invited and warmly welcomed. Over the last 30 years, their family has grown, with many grandchildren and now great-grandchildren. We always arrive before the scheduled noon meal to chat and socialize.</p><p>The patriarch is known for being eager to eat at the appointed time, but for the past three or four years, the matriarch has insisted no one begin eating until the final guest arrives — often 30 minutes to an hour late. As a guest, I'd never bring this up, not even to my wife, but I'm curious about your thoughts: Is it good manners to make those who arrive on time wait for those who can't seem to? — <i>FAMISHED FAMILY</i></p><p><b>DEAR FAMISHED:</b> No, it is not. The host should make every effort to begin the meal at the time mentioned in the invitation. Even so, latecomers should not be made to feel guilty; the in-progress meal will convey the message louder than words. The host should simply extend a warm welcome and a plate before returning to the more respectful guests.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.</p>

entries.title: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Rainbow PUSH celebrate Rev. Jesse Jackson’s birthday with youth conference
entries.summary: <p>The 10th District of Omega Psi Phi Fraternity honored the late Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr. on Saturday by hosting a youth leadership and STEM event aimed at carrying forward his commitment to civic engagement and education.</p><p>Held during Jackson’s birthday weekend, the event brought Chicago-area students to Rainbow PUSH Coalition for hands-on science activities and conversations about civic participation. Organizers said the programming reflected the values Jackson championed throughout his life and his deep ties to Omega Psi Phi, the fraternity he joined in 1960 and served in district and international leadership roles.</p><p>“Outside of our founders of Omega Psi Phi, Rev. Jackson has to be the most transcendent individual — not only in America, but in Omega Psi Phi — to have ever passed,” said Marquis Sagnia, the fraternity’s 39th 10th District representative.</p><p>Jackson’s relationship with the fraternity began before he became a member. James Felder, former South Carolina state representative, recalled <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/wbez-news/2026/03/06/how-greenville-south-carolina-shaped-jesse-jacksons-life-and-legacy-in-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>meeting Jackson as a child </u></a>through their mothers, who were both beauticians.</p><p>Felder said the fraternity’s members helped shape their childhoods, serving as mentors and role models. Their teachers, dentists and doctors were also members of Omega Psi Phi, he recalled.</p><p>“The men of Omega Psi Phi Fraternity — they were the people who motivated us, our advisors, our mentors,” Felder said.</p><p>All three civil rights giants — Jackson, Clyburn and Felder — eventually joined the organization that so heavily impacted them.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div entries.title: Block 37 owner is new, but is the curse still the same?
entries.summary: <p><i> In the Sun-Times last week: "Orland Park-based Edwards Realty Co.</i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/10/07/block-37-orland-park-edwards-realty-mall-rebrand-new-name" ><i> announced Wednesday </i></a><i>that it purchased Block 37 for $30 million, with plans to revamp the consumer experience at the Loop shopping mall."</i></p><p>True enough, though I would have gone with something along the lines of: </p><p></p><p></p><p>"You bought Block 37?!?!?! <i>Bwahaha!</i> Are you INSANE?"</p><p>A matter of tone, of course. The news routinely does — and very often should — reflect the dry facts set before the general public: leases and payments, business plans and company announcements.</p><p>But there is such a thing as karma. As juju. We could debate whether curses are real and whether certain physical places can be cursed for all time. The Bible endorses that notion, in Genesis: "Cursed is the ground for thy sake," God tells Adam, ejecting him from the Garden of Eden for, in his own way, failing to follow market imperatives. </p><p>How bad is it?</p><p>In the long history of urban development failure, there is really only one city block in the country that can be described as truly infamous: the block immediately east of Daley Plaza. Otherwise prime downtown property that has been known since before the city's founding as Block 37, it has also been called not only “cursed” but a "fiasco" and “a boondoggle.”</p><p>In 1996, a book was published chronicling earlier doomed efforts to make something take hold there. Ross Miller’s “Here’s the Deal,” cataloging years of lawsuits and protests over what he called a “gold-plated hole in the ground.”</p><p>Since then, a chain of false starts, bankruptcies, failures and foreclosures. Along with, to be fair, several modest successes: the studios of a once-respected television network, CBS on the southern half of the block. A popular restaurant, The Dearborn, on its northwest corner. Some offices and apartments.</p><p>And yet. One hopes Edwards Realty of Orland Park did their due diligence. But if not, buckle up guys, and sorry (<i>psst: note to regular readers. Not really sorry. In fact, I kinda dig it</i>) to be the one to have to tell you.</p><h3>In 1830, Block 37’s tale begins</h3><p>Like a good campfire story, the tale of Block 37 starts a long, long time ago, in 1830, and might indeed involve a Native American curse. Not because of the usual disturbed sacred burial ground,. But close. On the original map of Chicago, the ancestral land of the Council of the Three Fires, the Potawatomi, the Ojibwe and the Odawa, was platted up into 58 blocks so it could be sold off by New York real estate speculators to pay for the I & M Canal, thus permanently ripping off and disenfranchising the defrauded Indigenous peoples, who no doubt resented it. On that fateful document, the block delineated by Randolph, Washington, Dearborn and the edge of the map where State would someday run is designated with a number, and that number is 37.</p><div The original 1830 James Thompson map of Chicago. Block 37 is in the lower right, second from the bottom.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Wikimedia</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>It might be argued that Block 37 had a good 19th century. Office buildings. Theaters. A YMCA. Even the first half of the 20th century passed unstricken. There was a Stop & Shop. Maybe the curse was placed in 1989, when newly elected Mayor Richard M. Daley, hot to top his father as Rich the Builder, allowed the block to be razed, including the landmark McCarthy Building, a dear little five-story structure built the year after the Great Chicago Fire. Maybe that was the original sin, hubris: rejection of the past, clearing the entire block before its replacement was firmly set.</p><p>The site sat mostly empty for 20 years, poorly masked by various dismal half-efforts to hide its yawning vacancy in the heart of the Loop: a little-patronized ice skating rink; an underfunded arts and crafts festival, held in tents.</p><p>Starting in 2005, the CTA poured nearly half a billion dollars into the basement of Block 37, hoping to construct some sort of subterranean mega station tying the Blue and Red lines together. Instead, they only managed to create a really expensive cavern.</p><p>Finally, in 2009, a four-story mall opened that its owners called, with either laudable Chicago cheek or foolish strike-me-dead hubris, "Block Thirty Seven." That is what Edwards Realty of Orland Park boldly, or rashly, bought for $30 million.</p><p>For years, the place had a 70% vacancy rate. Though I worked nearby and passed frequently, I never considered going inside until one day in 2013 — this is how I described the experience:</p><p>"It says something about the outer Neptune orbital ring of Chicago consciousness" of the location that "the idea of actually stepping into an establishment on Block 37 never crossed my mind until Monday, after I noticed the Doughnut Vault’s distinctive cornflower-blue 1957 van parked on the sidewalk directly under the Dearborn entrance to what is boldly (or foolishly) called 'Block Thirty Seven Shops on State.' If Block 37 exerts a repulsive force on profits and customers, the Doughnut Vault is the opposite, exerting a magnetic, indeed, mesmeric, power. I bought a doughnut even though I wasn’t hungry and didn’t want one.</p><p>"I was chatting with Derek, the guy in the van, when a frantic publicist, seeing my notebook, waylaid me, insisting on personally escorting me that instant into Block 37. It all happened so quickly, it was a little discombobulating, as if a hatch opened in the Bean and a gnome yanked me inside. I would have preferred a bit of ceremony, the way buses entering Jerusalem will pause to let the occupants weep and sing and pray. The mall has been open four years, but the second floor has the raw feel of a space opening next month. There is one store."</p><p>I did my best to promote the desperate pop-up stores found inside, noting, "If you do go, after eating your fill, make sure you wander up to the third floor to gaze respectfully on the expanse of closed stores, noting the brave, sad mural showing the busy, successful food court that isn't there." </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div Even the future richest man in the world, who popularized the electric car and intends on colonizing Mars, saw his hopes come to nothing in Block 37.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Neil Steinberg/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3>‘Busy Rich Folks Underground Express’</h3><p>In 2018, then-mayor and now potential presidential candidate Rahm Emanuel held a press conference in the half-billion-dollar grotto carved deep below Block 37 with then car and space mogul and future poster boy for ethno-fascism Elon Musk, to announce their<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2018/6/14/18418853/zeppelins-monorails-and-now-rahm-s-rich-folks-underground-railroad" > $1 billion pipe dream </a>of boring a maglev train line to O'Hare Airport. What one wag — OK, me — immediately dubbed the "Busy Rich Folks Underground Express."</p><p>Almost needless to say, not a tablespoon of earth was ever turned over for that one.</p><p>Jumping to today: Is there no hope for the new owners of Block 37?</p><p>Seafarer Olivier Le Carrer, in his diverting "Atlas of Cursed Places" — which somehow overlooks Block 37 — divided such forlorn lands into three realms: those actually damned by specific spells or for being the loci of supernatural events; those blighted by nature — horrible climates, unquenchable fires, masses of sky-darkening bats, angry volcanoes.</p><p>And the third class, such as Block 37, places "rendered uninhabitable by human activity" of such an extreme nature as to bring "no real hope of change, the perenniality of the problem sadly being a key characteristic."</p><p>So is there no hope? entries.title: Hawi Feysa repeats as women's Chicago Marathon champion
entries.summary: <p>Hawi Feysa pulled away late to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon/2026/10/10/chicago-marathon-defending-champions-jacob-kiplimo-hawi-feysa-face-tough-tests-in-title-defense" >repeat as champion</a> of the women’s 2026 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon" >Chicago Marathon</a>.</p><p>Feysa and Sharon Lokedi were dueling into the last couple miles before Feysa ran away from Lokedi, winning the race at 2:13.33 for a new personal best. Lokedi came in second at 2:14.07.</p><p>Before Sunday, Ruth Chepngetich was the last woman to repeat as champion, winning in 2021 and 2022.</p><p>Brigid Kosgei, the 2018 and 2019 champion, finished third at 2:14.55.</p><h2><b>Women’s wheelchair division</b></h2><p>Catherine Debrunner reclaimed her title, winning in 1:33.16 to set a world record. The 2023 and 2024 winner, Debrunner finished ahead of second-place Tatyana McFadden (1:42.01).</p><p>By winning in Chicago, Debrunner continued her dominant 2026. The first-place Chicago medal joins the ones she’s earned in Tokyo, London and Berlin.</p><p>The 2025 champion, Susannah Scaroni was absent after having a child in August.</p>
entries.author: Brian Sandalow

entries.title: Amos Kipruto knocks off defending champion Jacob Kiplimo to win men's Chicago Marathon
entries.summary: <p>Having finished third in 2024 and second in 2025, Amos Kipruto hoped that trajectory would take him to the front of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon" >2026 Chicago Marathon</a>.</p><p>It did.</p><p>Kipruto took control in the second half of the race, beating <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon/2026/10/10/chicago-marathon-defending-champions-jacob-kiplimo-hawi-feysa-face-tough-tests-in-title-defense" >defending champion Jacob Kiplimo</a>. Kipruto finished in an unofficial time of 2:01.09, outpacing Kiplimo’s fourth-place time of 2:04.18. </p><p>Tadese Bikila finished second at 2:02.56.</p><p>For Kipruto, the win is his second at a major marathon, joining his 2022 win in London.</p><p>Kiplimo was attempting to become the first runner to repeat in the men’s division since Samuel Wanjiru pulled the double in 2009 and 2010.</p><h2><b>Men’s wheelchair division</b></h2><p>There was no suspense here, as Marcel Hug won for the fifth straight time. Hug, who has now won seven Chicago races, finished with an unofficial time of 1:21.33 to break his 2023 record of 1:22.37.</p><p>Lito Anker finished second in 1:30.11.</p><p>The racer who had the best chance to dethrone Hug was Daniel Romanchuk, a three-time champion. Unfortunately for Romanchuk, an early mechanical issue ended his race.</p>
entries.author: Brian Sandalow

entries.title: Bears wearing helmet decal honoring Mike Ditka vs. Packers
entries.summary: <p>The Bears will wear a helmet decal Sunday to honor Mike Ditka, who died Friday at age 86.</p><p>The decal will appear on the rear left corner of the Bears helmet. The navy decal, surrounded in orange, has a white No. 89 inside of it. Ditka wore the number as the Bears' Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end. His number was the last one the Bears retired before stopping the practice because they were running out of numbers to give active players.</p><p>The decal tribute is similar to what the Bears did Steve McMichael when he died last year.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="und" dir="ltr">For 89 💙 <a href="https://t.co/0pynPgHoBb">pic.twitter.com/0pynPgHoBb</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2109281217136730378?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Bears had a patch for Dick Butkus when he died. The Bears plan to have further tributes for Ditka the next time they play at home — Oct. 22 against the Patriots.</p><p>Ditka died Friday, prompting tributes from around the NFL, pop culture and the Bears. Coach Ben Johnson called Ditka the "gold standard" inside Halas Hall.</p>

entries.title: Connor Bedard's return to Blackhawks suddenly seems imminent: 'I feel really confident'
entries.summary: <p>Connor Bedard's return to the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>' lineup suddenly appears fairly imminent.</p><p>The 21-year-old Hawks captain practiced with the team Sunday in a regular red jersey, shedding the black non-contact jersey he donned last week, and he took some light contact in drills without issue.</p><p>Coach Jeff Blashill said Bedard will have a doctor's appointment sometime this week in which his surgically repaired left shoulder will be examined and his first game date will be determined.</p><p>Blashill added he couldn't completely rule out Bedard for Tuesday against the Penguins. After that, the Hawks host the Jets on Thursday and the Stars on Saturday, then have a six-day break before facing the Canadiens on Oct. 23.</p><p>"People here see me every day, on the gym, on the ice, and you test [the shoulder], you see where it's at," Bedard said Sunday. "Everyone was confident with the contact aspect of getting in a full skate and that unpredictability of what's going to happen out there. </p><p>"I feel really confident in it, and I think they do, as well, to let me do that. [I] just hope to keep getting that exposure, and obviously [I] want to play as soon as possible."</p><p>The second-most notable part of practice — beyond the color of Bedard's jersey — was that he skated as the first-line center between Patrick Kane and Roman Kantserov.</p><p>That's likely where he will slot into the Hawks' lineup when he returns, and the fact he participated in line rushes at all is another sign the Hawks expect that moment to be soon. Blashill said the timing of the practice — with another one scheduled Monday — made it doable.</p><p>"Obviously, he’s getting closer. Otherwise, we wouldn’t start making that progress," Blashill said. "We’ll see how it goes."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Connor Bedard vs. Bowen Byram in a light contact drill <a href="https://t.co/8CK66OYjLp">pic.twitter.com/8CK66OYjLp</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2109317527603982645?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Bedard, being his usual supportive self, said he has seen the Hawks "doing a lot of good things" on the ice even though their 1-5-0 record doesn't reflect it.</p><p>There's no doubt his return will make a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/10/07/blackhawks-connor-bedard-injury-update-practice" >huge difference</a>, though, not only with the injection of his elite offensive skills but also because his presence will allow every other forward — some of whom are over-slotted right now — to move down a rung in the depth chart.</p><p>He will be able to take faceoffs right away, too, which wasn't the case when he returned from his right shoulder injury last winter.</p><p>"It’s almost more frustrating near the end of [the recovery] than the start of it," Bedard said. "[At] the start of it, you’re like, 'I can’t even move my arm, so there’s nothing I can really do.' </p><p>"I feel normal. I feel like myself shooting the puck, [doing] everything. You want to play. I wanted to play Game One. But obviously, you want to be safe, as well. [I'm] working with a lot of great people, coming in every day and grinding, trying to get it back as soon as possible. Once they feel like it’s in a good spot, then I’ll be back out there."</p><p>The Hawks' power play might need Bedard more than anything. They're 1-for-14 this season, having barely even threatened. </p><p>Blashill said Bedard might slot in the left side, allowing Kane to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/21/blackhawks-power-play-patrick-kane-roman-kantserov-bowen-byram" >move back</a> to his natural right side and positioning both of them for one-timers.</p><p>It will also be interesting how the Hawks construct their new second line during five-on-five play. entries.title: Pope Leo to undergo lung surgery
entries.summary: <p>VATICAN CITY — <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/pope-leo-xiv" target="_blank" >Pope Leo XIV</a> announced Sunday he will undergo surgery this week to remove a nodular lesion on his lung, in the first major health event of <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/conclave-pope-francis-cardinals-vatican-d7991a37a679f09792ed220cc1f6bbed" target="_blank" >his 17-month pontificate.</a></p><p>The 71-year-old Leo said the nodule was found at an early stage and was “circumscribed” or well-localized. The Vatican said Leo would undergo surgery in ”the coming days," with an expected recovery time of a week.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/trump-leo-prevost-american-chicago-immigration-94080518606f7b56abfb818f573d625b" target="_blank" >The American pope</a> made the announcement during his Sunday noon blessing. He thanked the crowd for their closeness and entrusted himself to their prayers.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Dear friends, during some recent medical examinations, the doctors found a small, localized nodule in my lung. It was detected at a very early stage and is well-localized. The doctors believe that it is best to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo…</p>— Pope Leo XIV (@Pontifex) <a href="https://x.com/Pontifex/status/2109267778553221597?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3>A nodule can be benign or malignant</h3><p>A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 1 inch that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen, according to the American Cancer Society. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening.</p><p>“Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign, but benign and cancerous nodules can have a similar appearance on imaging," said Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center.</p><p>"When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis,” he said in an email.</p><p>Leo has no previously known health problems and is physically active, with weekly tennis matches and swimming at the papal summer retreat in Castel Gandolfo.</p><p>The pope has a major trip planned Nov. 6-17 to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It's unclear how or whether the planned surgery and recovery might affect the itinerary, but Leo said earlier in his remarks Sunday he still planned to go.</p><p>In his remarks, delivered in Italian, Leo said that during a recent medical check, “doctors found a small, localized nodule in my lung. It was detected at a very early stage and is circumscribed. The doctors believe it’s best to take action, so, following their advice, I have decided to have surgery to remove it."</p><p>He thanked the faithful "for your spiritual support, and I entrust myself to your prayers.”</p><h3>Surgery to be at the pope’s hospital</h3><p>Leo’s predecessor, <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/pope-francis-remembrance-life-7702c44513ed4c9ba0ac5362d418c3f4" target="_blank" >Pope Francis, died April 21, 2025,</a> of a stroke following a long hospitalization brought on by a respiratory crisis that developed into double pneumonia. <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/vatican-pope-health-timeline-b3097d79a3f61d93b0b26def7dd9a6da" target="_blank" >Francis suffered from chronic lung disease</a> and had part of one lung removed as a young man.</p><p>Leo is expected to undergo surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital, where Francis and popes before him were treated and where there is a special apartment for pontiffs.</p><p>Dr. Massimo Di Maio, president of the Italian Association of Medical Oncology, said it will be important to determine if the nodule is benign or malignant, and if it is malignant, whether it has spread. When the disease is detected at an early stage “the aim … is curative,” he added.</p><p>Depending on what is found, possible treatments can include chemotherapy and radiation therapy, Di Maio told Italy’s private Sky TG24.</p><p>“When we talk about something being localized, that can also refer to the need to establish whether the disease is confined to that one site or whether scans show signs of disease elsewhere,” he said, adding he has not treated the pope and was speaking about the disease in general.</p><p>“Being physically fit and healthy is certainly an important starting point for coping as well as possible with treatment, including surgery,” he added.</p><p>Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni, among the few outsiders to visit Francis during his long final hospitalization, expressed her support, and that of the Italian government, for Leo “as he faces this challenge in the coming days.” In a statement, she added “the serenity and calm with which he spoke about it” were reassuring.</p>

entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> made starting quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/08/31/why-do-so-many-people-hate-bears-qb-caleb-williams-he-answers-exactly-that-question" >Caleb Williams</a> inactive Sunday against the Packers, but now that he’s gotten back on the practice field, he could return next week against the Falcons.</p><p>The team did not designate him as its emergency quarterback, meaning he will not play under any circumstances.</p><p>Williams has been out since suffering a Grade 2 hamstring strain Sept. 20 against the Vikings. He did some throwing workouts last week, then partially participated in practice Friday. The Bears listed him as questionable for the Packers game, indicating they were uncertain whether he’d be available, which was odd given that coach Ben Johnson said at the beginning of the week that Tyson Bagent would start.</p><p>Regardless, barring any setback, Williams appears to be on track to step back into his spot when practice resumes Wednesday. He worked out before the game, mainly taking snaps and dropping back to focus on footwork.</p><p>The Bears are heading into a tight, Sunday-Thursday turnaround, however, and might opt against putting Williams through that as he recovers from the injury. They play at the Falcons on Sunday, then host the Patriots on Oct. 22.</p><p>If there’s still any concern about his leg, it’d be more prudent to give him a few extra days and bring him back against the Patriots. The Bears also have an extended break after that game before visiting the defending champion Seahawks on Nov. 2, which makes that a much more favorable on ramp for Williams.</p><p>It’s already notable that Williams has missed three starts after rarely missing a snap his first two seasons. He started 38 consecutive games, including playoffs, to begin his career and played 99% of the snaps each of his first two seasons.</p><p>He went into this season with enormous expectations <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/01/money-isnt-everything-with-a-big-contract-in-reach-qb-caleb-williams-wants-to-make-sure-bears-keep-winning" target="_blank" >and the chance to earn a long-term contract extension</a>, and got off to a great start with one of the sharpest games of his career against the Panthers. He was struggling against the Vikings before going down with the hamstring injury in the fourth quarter.</p><p>Here are the Bears’ inactives against the Packers:</p><p>QB Caleb Williams (hamstring)<br>RB Kyle Monangai (toe)<br>OT Ozzy Trapilo</p><p>DL Jayden Loving<br>LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad)<br>DL Jamree Kromah</p>

entries.title: Vikings top Saints 23-13 to remain unbeaten
entries.summary: <p>NEW ORLEANS — Justin Jefferson highlighted his return to Minnesota's lineup with a leaping touchdown catch, Aaron Jones made up for an early fumble with a pivotal, fourth-quarter touchdown and the Vikings remained unbeaten with a 23-13 victory over the slumping New Orleans Saints on Sunday.</p><p>Will Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts from 40 or more yards for the Vikings (5-0), including a 55-yarder to put Minnesota up 10 in the fourth quarter and all but doom the Saints (1-4) to a third straight loss — all in the Superdome.</p><p>Jones finished with 113 yards rushing on 25 carries. Jefferson, who sat out Week 4 with an ankle injury, caught six passes for 79 yards from Kyler Murray, who threw for 229 yards and a TD without a turnover and rushed for 51 yards.</p><p>The Vikings, who came in allowing an NFL-low 12.8 points per game, gave up only one offensive touchdown and held New Orleans to 142 yards.</p><p>Safety Jonas Sanker returned a fumble 87 yards for the Saints' other TD.</p><p>Both teams were plagued by turnovers.</p><p>Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was intercepted twice and held to 96 yards passing. New Orleans also lost a fumble — and ultimately, a 7-6 halftime lead — when returner Jayden Price was stripped on the kickoff to open the second half.</p><p>Minnesota took over on the Saints 37 and cashed in when Jefferson came down with Murray's 15-yard scoring pass behind three defenders in the back of the end zone.</p><p>The Saints turned the ball over again soon after, when Shough threw while rolling right and was intercepted by Byron Murphy Jr. near midfield. But Minnesota's Myles Price fumbled it back to Sanker, whose return tied it at 13 — a score that held after kicker Daniel Carlson missed an extra point.</p><p>Minnesota was threatening to widen a 3-0 lead when Jones lost a fumble on the New Orleans 7. Chase Young recovered, returning the ball to the Saints 34, and the drive culminated with Kendre Miller's 2-yard touchdown run.</p><p>Reichard hit his second field goal of the game — from 54 yards — as the half ended.</p><h3>Drew Brees received his Hall of Fame ring</h3><p>Retired Saints QB Drew Brees was honored with a ring ceremony at halftime — and also had his name unveiled in the team's Ring of Honor, which encircles the upper deck.</p><p>Brees received a rousing ovation as he was introduced on the field, wearing his gold Hall of Fame jacket, and presented his ring by Pro Football Hall of Fame president Jim Porter.</p><p>"It has been one of the greatest honors of my life to be able to represent this city, this community, this fan base and our organization," Brees said. "I will always love you, New Orleans. I will always represent you."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p>Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson was helped off the field after hitting his head hard on the turf while being tackled during a 7-yard catch.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Vikings:</b> Enter their bye week before hosting Indianapolis on Oct. 25.</p><p><b>Saints:</b> Visit the New York Giants next Sunday.<br></p>

Seriously, who could pick?</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACKS — F</b></h3><p>Remember that hilarious narrative about the Bears having not one, not two, but three good players at the most important position in all of sports? Man, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-bench-qb-tyson-bagent-after-two-interceptions-vs-packers-then-case-keenum-throws-one-too" >what a hoot that was.</a> It’s hard to guess what Tyson Bagent spent the previous week doing, but it can’t have been preparing to face the Packers. Even when he wasn’t gifting the ball to Packers safety Xavier McKinney — one interception thrown smack into double coverage, the other thrown behind Colston Loveland — he was off target and anything but in command. Case Keenum came in for the fourth quarter and promptly added a pick to the Packers’ pile, and later lost a fumble. Where you at, Caleb Williams? Your services are desperately needed.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE BACKS — F</b></h3><p>Somewhere along the way, Packers QB Jordan Love found wide receiver Christian Watson for a 31-yard gain. The point? Hard to believe this could happen, but it was merely Love’s <i>sixth</i>-longest pass of the game. Xavier Woods got spun like a top on Watson’s 42-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Dillon Thieneman was inside Watson’s jersey on a 53-yard touchdown yet somehow failed to make any play on the ball whatsoever. Malik Muhammad got torched on a 46-yarder to tight end Tucker Kraft. Jaylon Johnson gave up his share of big ones — is he fast enough anymore? — and got absolutely run over by MarShawn Lloyd on the running back’s six-yard touchdown rumble.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE LINE — D-PLUS</b></h3><p>Here’s looking at you, Austin Booker, you two-sack haver, you. Alas, nobody else got after Love or else he wouldn’t have had time to luxuriate in the pocket before chucking all those long balls. Pretty sure Love was spotted sipping from an umbrella drink before one of the heaves.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — C</b></h3><p>File Zavion Thomas’ 61-yard kickoff return in the back of your head; at some point this season, he’ll bust a big one that’ll really mean something. Cairo Santos was wide left on a 43-yard field-goal attempt, which didn’t mean much by the end a miserable day for the team but kept the Bears from closing to 20-10 — which wouldn’t have seemed hopeless at the time.</p><h3><b>COACHING — F</b></h3><p>Western scholars will ruminate for many years on which was worse Sunday, the Bears’ offense or their defense. But this was all kinds of awful. Ben Johnson can hate the Packers all he wants, but they still tortured him on what had to be the worst day of his head coaching life. The Bears were unprepared. They made a million bad mistakes. What an embarrassing display.</p>
entries.author: Steve Greenberg

entries.title: Packers QB Jordan Love dominates Bears defense with deep shots
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> dared Jordan Love to beat them deep.</p><p>The Packers quarterback did, over and over again, in a 31-7 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/packers-lead-bears-14-7-at-halftime-at-lambeau-field-after-costly-tyson-bagent-interception" target="_blank" >rivalry loss</a> Sunday at Lambeau Field.</p><p>A Bears defense that dominated the previous three weeks — they gave up nine points in the rain to the Vikings, seven to the Eagles and 12 to the Jets — looked more like the unit that produced a disturbing season opening performance. When the Bears gave up 37 points to the Panthers, it seemed like the start of a long, frustrating season for the defense.</p><p>It felt that way again Sunday. Bears coordinator Dennis Allen stubbornly stuck with his man defense — and paid dearly for it. He lost a starter at each level of his defense to injury during the game — Dayo Odeyingbo (quad), linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring) — but the Packers were in charge from the beginning. </p><p>One week after Love threw for just 197 yards and totaled 17 points against the Buccaneers, the Packers scored touchdowns on their first two drives. Love finished 25-for-31 for 367 yards, two touchdowns and a 137.5 passer rating. He completed 6-of-8 passes of 20 yards or more, totaling 258 yards and a near-perfect 156.3 passer rating.</p><p>The scoring started with a 42-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson in the first quarter when a blown coverage left him wide open down the left sideline. In the third quarter alone, the Bears gave up a 46-yard pass to tight end Tucker Kraft and a 36-yard pass to Matthew Golden. And then, in the fourth quarter, a 50-yarder to Golden.</p><p>In between was the most egregious series of plays the Bears defense has posted this season.</p><p>Love thought he’d thrown a 43-yard touchdown down the right sideline to receiver J. Michael Sturdivant about two minutes into the second half. Sturdivant was whistled for offensive pass interference, though, which left the Packers facing third-and-22 at their own 47. On the next play, Love dropped back and with all the time in the world, stepped up in the pocket. He launched a pass deep down the middle to receiver Christian Watson, who’d slipped behind the back line of the Bears defense. As the ball hung in the air, rookie safety ran underneath the ball. Watson leapt and caught the ball for a 53-yard touchdown.</p><p>Love threw the ball from his own 40 — and it landed in Watson’s arms about three yards beyond the goal line.</p><p>Before Sunday, the Bears had defended third-and-22 or more 219 times since 1977. They’d never given up a play so long.</p><p>The Packers, as true rivals, kept throwing long after the game was in control. The Bears could do very little to stop it.</p><p>The performance was needed in Green Bay, where a 2-2 start prompted questions from a frustrated fan base that questioned not only Love but play-caller and head coach Matt LaFleur. For the Bears, though, though, Sunday opens up defensive questions that had been on hold for a month.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Bears stumble throughout embarrassing 31-7 loss to Packers amid turnovers by Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Throughout the partnership between <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson and quarterback Caleb Williams, the emphasis has been overwhelmingly on what Johnson can do for Williams.</p><p>But it’s a symbiotic relationship, and the coach desperately needs his quarterback back.</p><p>Johnson has kept the Bears afloat <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-qb-caleb-williams-inactive-vs-packers-but-appears-on-track-to-return-for-falcons-game" >in Williams’ absence</a>, but there have been too many times when the offense sputtered and neither Johnson nor backup quarterback Tyson Bagent could ignite it. That was the case Sunday for most of the Bears’ 31-7 loss to the Packers at Lambeau Field.</p><p>It was the team’s first game since the death of former coach Mike Ditka on Friday, and players wore a No. 89 decal on their helmets in honor of the number he wore as a Bears tight end in the 1960s. The Packers held a moment of silence for Ditka before the game.</p><p>It was evident early that the offense was in for a rough day without Williams and backup running back Kyle Monangai, who was the engine a week earlier by rushing for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries to compensate for a mediocre performance by Bagent.</p><p>No one saved the day Sunday, though, as Bagent completed 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards and two interceptions for a 27.4 passer rating before Johnson benched him for Case Keenum early in the fourth quarter.</p><p>Keenum was no better. He walked into a golden opportunity with the Bears starting at the Packers’ 31-yard line and squandered it by throwing an interception in the end zone on fourth-and-goal. He also lost a fumble in the fourth.</p><p>No one had an answer, including Johnson.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears bench QB Tyson Bagent after two interceptions vs. Packers, then Case Keenum throws one, too
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson benched quarterback Tyson Bagent in the fourth quarter Sunday after the team fell behind 31-7 against the Packers. Case Keenum took over with 14:47 remaining.</p><p>Bagent, starting for injured quarterback Caleb Williams, never got the offense in rhythm and sunk the Bears with two interceptions. He completed 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards and exited with a 27.4 passer rating.</p><p>Keenum got a good opportunity starting at the Packers’ 31-yard line after rookie Zavion Thomas’ 61-yard kick return. He completed his first two passes to get the Bears to the 3-yard line, but threw an interception in the end zone on fourth-and-goal from the 10.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-qb-caleb-williams-inactive-vs-packers-but-appears-on-track-to-return-for-falcons-game" >The Bears now hope Williams will return Sunday to face the Falcons in Atlanta</a>. He progressed from throwing on the side last week to practicing partially Friday to working out at Lambeau Field on Sunday morning and appears to be on track to step back into his spot when the team resumes practice Wednesday.</p><p>Williams worked on taking snaps under center, dropping back, handing off and throwing deep in his workout in Green Bay and moved well.</p>

entries.title: On live radio, frustrated Ben Johnson says Bears must be '[bleeping] better'
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — A frustrated Ben Johnson said the Bears needed to "be f———g" better on the radio as he ran to the locker room for halftime of the Bears-Packers game Sunday at Lambeau Field. </p><p>The Bears head coach was being interviewed by ESPN 1000 sideline reporter Jason McKie after the first half wound down with the Bears down 14-7. He was asked about momentum.</p><p>“Momentum, shmo-mentum," Johnson said. "We gotta play f———g better. Gotta be f——-ng better”</p><p>The cursing on live radio was, perhaps, a turn of phrase that late Bears coach Mike Ditka would have appreciated.</p><p>The Bears trailed the Packers 14-0 before scoring on a one-yard D'Andre Swift run late in the first half. They then pushed the Packers out of field goal range with the help of two Austin Booker sacks and an illegal substitution penalty against Green Bay. </p>

entries.title: Northwestern moves into AP Top 25; Georgia takes over at No. 1
entries.summary: <p>Georgia moved up to No. 1 in The Associated Press Top 25 on Sunday following its win at Alabama, Texas dropped six spots to No. 7 after its loss to rival Oklahoma and Oregon was unranked for the first time in four years after losing for the second time in the past month. And Northwestern entered the rankings for the first time under coach David Braun.</p><p>The Bulldogs, who had been No. 2 for five straight polls while rolling off five straight lopsided wins, went on the road and beat Alabama 20-17 with the help of what appeared to be a missed pass interference call in the end zone late in the game.</p><p>Georgia received 66 first-place votes from the panel of 70 media members after its first victory in Tuscaloosa since 2014 and ascended to the top of the poll for the first time since Sept. 8, 2024.</p><p>Notre Dame, which tuned up for this week's top-10 matchup at BYU with a 58-7 rout of Stanford, moved up one spot to No. 2. The Fighting Irish got one first-place vote and have their highest ranking since they were No. 2 in the final poll of the 2024 season.</p><p>No. 3 Miami, which received two first-place votes, is followed by Ohio State and Indiana. The Hoosiers, who received the remaining first-place vote, got a two-spot promotion after their narrow win at Nebraska.</p><p>Alabama remained No. 6, and Texas, BYU, Mississippi and Texas Tech completed the top 10.</p><p>Oregon came into the season with its highest preseason ranking ever at No. 2. The Ducks' turnover-fueled 17-15 home loss to UCLA dropped them to 3-2 and knocked them out of the poll for the first time since they went from No. 11 to unranked following a 49-3 loss to Georgia in the 2022 opener.</p><p>No. 12 UCLA and No. 15 Kentucky got the biggest promotions. The Bruins moved up nine spots with their win over Oregon, and the Wildcats went from unranked to No. 15 with their 35-34 overtime win over LSU, which dropped from No. 10 to No. 22.</p><h3>In and out</h3><h3></h3><p>In: Kentucky, which dropped out last week after beating South Carolina, is back in the poll with its highest ranking since early October 2022.</p><p>In: No. 21 Wake Forest is 5-1 and ranked for the first time since late October 2022.</p><p>In: No. 25 Northwestern, at 4-1, earned its first ranking under fourth-year coach David Braun.</p><p>Out: Oregon hasn't lost two of its first five games since the 2016 team opened 2-5 and finished 4-8.</p><p>Out: Florida has gone from No. 8 to No. 16 to out of the rankings in two weeks following its 38-19 home loss to South Carolina.</p><p>Out: Pittsburgh managed just one touchdown on eight second-half possessions in a 21-17 home loss to North Carolina.</p><h3>Poll points</h3><h3></h3><p>• This is the second time in three years there have been three or more No. 1 teams in the first six polls. Georgia, Texas and Alabama took turns holding the top spot in the first six polls in 2024. The only other time in the Top 25 era that three teams had been No. 1 at this point of a season was 1990.</p><p>• Notre Dame and Miami, dubbed "Catholic vs. Convicts" rivals since their classic game in 1988, haven't been together in the top three since Nov. 9, 1993.</p><p>• Texas' six-spot fall from No. 1 to No. 7 matched its drop following a season-opening loss to Ohio State last year.</p><h3>Conference call</h3><h3></h3><p><b>SEC (9 ranked teams):</b> No. 1 Georgia, No. 6 Alabama, No. 7 Texas, No. 9 Mississippi, No. 13 Missouri, No. 14 Tennessee, No. 15 Kentucky, No. 16 Mississippi State, No. 22 LSU.</p><p><b>Big Ten (6):</b> No. 4 Ohio State, No. 5 Indiana, No. 12 UCLA, No. 17 Iowa, No. 19 USC, No. 25 Northwestern.</p><p><b>Big 12 (5):</b> No. 8 BYU, No. 10 Texas Tech, No. 11 Utah, No. 18 Oklahoma State, No. 20 Houston.</p><p><b>ACC (3):</b> No. 3 Miami, No. 21 Wake Forest, No. 24 SMU.</p><p><b>Pac-12 (1):</b> No. 23 Boise State.</p><p><b>Independent (1):</b> No. 3 Notre Dame.</p><h3>Ranked vs. ranked</h3><h3></h3><p><b>No. 4 Ohio State at No. 5 Indiana:</b> Ohio State plays its second top-five matchup of the season. entries.title: Boyfriend charged with murder after woman found fatally stabbed in Chicago Lawn
entries.summary: <p>A man was charged with first-degree murder after his girlfriend was fatally stabbed Friday night in Chicago Lawn, Chicago police said.</p><p>Gustavo Soto, 46, was arrested in Gage Park three hours after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/09/woman-fatally-stabbed-during-argument-in-chicago-lawn" target="_blank" >he was allegedly arguing</a> with a 48-year-old woman, pulled out a knife and fatally stabbed her, according to police. The woman has not been identified, but police said she was Soto's girlfriend.</p><p>Soto was expected to make his first court appearance Sunday.</p>

entries.title: Chicago Marathon supporters encourage runners at Mile 22 to get to the finish line
entries.summary: <p>Equipped with more than 6,000 bottles of water, plastic trumpets and a DJ booth, Chloe Wilkerson, 34, and her family were ready Sunday morning for the thousands of runners to pass by the support station they had set up at Mile 22 of the Chicago Marathon.</p><p>Wilkerson’s family was stationed on 26th Street near Michigan Avenue, an area that sees some of the smallest crowds despite it being one of the most mentally taxing parts of the 26.2-mile race.</p><p>“We're gonna give them as much encouragement as we can,” Wilkerson said.</p><p>Supporters blared music, sanitation workers rang cowbells, and children shook tambourines while Taylor Swift, Bruno Mars and Chicago house music boomed in the background.</p><p>Chris Bennett, Nike running global head coach, said Wilkerson’s family, along with support from others along both sides of the street, is what make Mile 22 special.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item"> entries.title: Amos Kipruto finally wins men's Chicago Marathon, joining three familiar gold medalists as 2026 champions
entries.summary: <p>Winning their divisions in Sunday’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon" >Chicago Marathon</a> was a familiar feeling for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon/2026/10/10/chicago-marathon-defending-champions-jacob-kiplimo-hawi-feysa-face-tough-tests-in-title-defense" >2026 women’s champion Hawi Feysa</a>, women’s wheelchair titlist Catherine Debrunner and men’s wheelchair gold medalist Marcel Hug.</p><p>That was not the case for men’s champion Amos Kipruto.</p><p>Having finished third in 2024 and second in 2025, Kipruto hoped that trajectory would take him to the front Sunday. It did, and resulted in a personal best time of 2:01.09. That speed pushed Kipruto past defending champion Jacob Kiplimo, who finished fourth at 2:04.18 and was unable to become the first men’s repeat winner since Samuel Wanjiru pulled the double in 2009 and 2010.</p><p>Kipruto didn’t need to be reminded of his past performance in Chicago. Due to his familiarity with the course, he was optimistic earlier in the week he would move up to the first spot.</p><p>He proved that feeling was correct, adding the Chicago gold medal to the one he picked up in 2022 in London. Kipruto beat second-place finisher Tadese Bikila (2:02.56) by almost two minutes, giving him time to savor the win and push for a personal best.</p><p>“I was ready,” Kipruto said.</p><p>There was no doubting Feysa’s readiness, either.</p><p>Despite coming in as the defending champion, Feysa was somewhat overshadowed by the return of Brigid Kosgei, the 2018 and 2019 winner. Feysa and Sharon Lokedi pulled away from Kosgei, and then Feysa separated from Lokedi to win the race at 2:13.33 for a new personal best.</p><p>Lokedi came in second at 2:14.07 and Kosgei’s third-place time was 2:14.55. Through a translator Feysa said the race was “hard-fought” in the latter stages but was confident around the 35-kilometer mark she would win.</p><p>“It means everything to come here and win again,” Feysa said.</p><p>Debrunner added a little bit of history to her win.</p><p>The 2023 and 2024 winner in Chicago, Debrunner set a world record with her time of 1:33.16. By winning in Chicago, Debrunner continued her dominant 2026. The first-place Chicago medal joins the ones she’s earned in Tokyo, London and Berlin.</p><p>The world-record time was somewhat surprising because Chicago is considered a technical wheelchair course because of its turns. The potholes city drivers know too well can also be a factor.</p><p>None of that stopped Debrunner, who finished almost nine minutes ahead of second-place Tatyana McFadden (1:42.01).</p><p>“[To break] world records, everything needs to be perfect. Especially the weather, [which] plays a really big role,” Debrunner said. “It seems that today it all came together.”</p><p>Hug has experienced that before in Chicago, and a lot of other places.</p><p>Sunday was Hug’s fifth straight Chicago win and seventh overall. He set a new course record of 1:21.34, passing the mark of 1:22.37 he set in 2023. His win Sunday added to a stocked trophy case that includes 10 wins in Berlin and eight in London.</p><p>“Today was a great day for us. Great conditions,” Hug said. “I’m really happy with my performance today. [It maybe] was one of the best performances of my career today.”</p>
