entries.title: Lions' offense romps in a 45-21 win over the Cardinals
entries.summary: <p>GLENDALE, Ariz. — Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, Jahmyr Gibbs added 151 yards rushing and two more scores and the Detroit Lions shook off a slow start by scoring 31 straight points to roll past the Arizona Cardinals 45-21 on Sunday.</p><p>Gibbs barreled into the end zone on a 1-yard run in the second quarter and added a 3-yard TD run in the fourth, bouncing off the offensive line before reversing field and finding room to run. The three-time Pro Bowl selection has scored an NFL-record 58 touchdowns before his 25th birthday, passing Lions great Barry Sanders, who had 57.</p><p>Jameson Williams had his first multi-TD receiving game, catching touchdowns for 8 and 39 yards for Detroit (3-2).</p><p>Arizona (1-4) has lost nine straight home games, a streak that's lasted more than a year.</p><p>It was a disappointing, weird afternoon for the Cardinals, who finalized a trade to send receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in the middle of the first quarter. Harrison was one of the team's five inactives against the Lions and wasn't seen at the stadium.</p><p>The No. 4 overall pick in 2024 out of Ohio State has been a major disappointment in the desert and he had just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown through four games this season.</p><p>But the non-Harrison version of the Cardinals wasn't any better Sunday.</p><p>Arizona took an early 7-0 lead after a 2-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett to tight end Teagan Quitoriano, but right about the time news of the Harrison deal started spreading, the momentum shifted.</p><p>Detroit scored three straight touchdowns and a field goal to take a 24-7 lead into halftime. Tight end Sam LaPorta caught the second of the three TDs, finding himself wide open for a 38-yard catch and run.</p><p>Williams added a 39-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter on a perfectly-thrown ball by Goff, who completed 19 of 30 passes for 279 yards. Goff also ran for a 1-yard touchdown.</p><p>While the Lions were piling up points, the Cardinals had five straight three-and-out drives during the first half, gaining just 12 total yards. On the sixth drive, Brissett threw an interception that ended the second quarter.</p><p>It was a better performance by the Lions' defense, which came into Sunday giving up 31.8 points per game to rank No. 31 in the NFL.</p><p>Brissett completed 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. He is 2-15 as the team's starter since taking over for Kyler Murray last season.</p><p>Quitoriano finished with two receiving touchdowns, adding a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Trey McBride also had a 9-yard TD catch late in the fourth quarter.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Lions:</b> LB Devin White (forearm) and KR/PR Tom Kennedy (knee) both left the game and didn't return.</p><p><b>Cardinals:</b> S Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) was hurt late in the first half.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Lions:</b> Host Green Bay on Oct. 25.</p><p><b>Cardinals:</b> At the Los Angeles Rams next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Bears QB Case Keenum encourages Tyson Bagent: Getting 'ass kicked' is all about response
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> and Tyson Bagent have waited years for him to get an opportunity to be their starting quarterback, especially in coach Ben Johnson’s offense, but it’s been rough so far.</p><p></p><p>Bagent was bad enough <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-coach-ben-johnson-runs-out-of-answers-unable-to-ignite-offense-in-31-7-loss-to-packers" >in the 31-7 loss to the Packers on Sunday</a> to get benched as Johnson ran out of patience waiting for him to get the offense rolling. He completed 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards with two interceptions for a 27.4 passer rating, and Keenum was more of the same at 11-for-19 passing, 108 yards, an interception, a lost fumble and a 52.1 passer rating.</p><p></p><p>Johnson wouldn’t say which quarterback would start Sunday at the Falcons if Caleb Williams remains out. Williams practiced — he was limited — Friday for the first time since suffering a Grade 2 hamstring strain Sept. 20 against the Vikings.</p><p></p><p>He pulled Bagent immediately after the second interception, which Bagent attributed to misreading the Packers’ coverage. They showed Cover 0 before the snap, then flipped to Cover 2, and Bagent didn’t recognize it quickly enough. It was a day full of mistakes, and he took accountability.</p><p></p><p>“You would definitely not want to be benched, especially with the opportunity that I've been blessed with, but ... I’ve got to play better,” Bagent said. “I’ve got to look in the mirror, see where I can continue to get better, because there's a lot of things still, even this far into my career, that I can certainly get better at.”</p><p></p><p>Who better than Keenum to encourage him to be resilient?</p><p></p><p>Keenum, 38, is on his ninth team in 15 seasons and has bounced around the league as both a starter and backup. Before his epic “Monday Night Football” victory over the Eagles, he thought he’d never get a chance to play again, let alone start.</p><p></p><p>When asked after the game Sunday what he said to Bagent, Keenum preferred to keep that private, but gave a glimpse into his message.</p><p></p><p>“You don’t last very long in this league if you don’t know how to get back up when you’ve had your ass kicked,” Keenum said. “That’s just the way it is. There’s really good players, really good coaches, really good teams, and if you last long enough, it’s just a matter of time that you’re going to get your ass kicked.</p><p></p><p>“It’s not about that. It’s about how you respond. I expect him to respond like he knows how to. It’s adversity to learn from. It’s an opportunity to learn from your mistakes and move on and not make them again.”</p>

entries.title: Man charged with fatally stabbing CTA janitor at Green Line station
entries.summary: <p>A 37-year-man was charged with murder after a Chicago Transit Authority janitor was fatally stabbed last Thursday at the Damen Green Line station, according to authorities.</p><p>Chevazz Campbell of Kenwood <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/09/its-terrible-said-mom-of-cta-janitor-slain-while-helping-injured-co-worker-at-near-west-side-green-line" target="_blank" >turned himself in last week</a> after Julian Mobley was attacked when he tried to help another CTA staffer who was allegedly pepper-sprayed by Campbell.</p><p>In addition to murder, Campbell faces charges for robbery, possession of weapon, carrying a weapon on CTA and fare evasion. He was expected to make his first court appearance Sunday.</p><p>When Mobley tried to help the staffer who had been attacked and pepper-sprayed, Campbell allegedly stabbed Mobley in the back of his neck with a pair of scissors. Mobley was taken to Stroger Hospital and pronounced dead a short time later. A Friday autopsy determined he died of a stab wound to his neck, and his death was ruled a homicide, according to the Cook County medical examiner’s office.</p>

entries.title: Bears' post-Ditka-era misery at Lambeau Field resumes as Packers revel in 31-7 beatdown
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Well, that was a real kick in the keister.</p><p>“Green Bay sucks,” does it?</p><p>Chicago sports fans can chant that until they’re blue in the face. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson can “hate” the bleepin’ Packers all he wants. Anyone still pointing to the Bears’ two wins in this rivalry last season, the second one coming in the playoffs, can knock themselves out.</p><p>But we all just saw the same thing — a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/packers-lead-bears-14-7-at-halftime-at-lambeau-field-after-costly-tyson-bagent-interception" target="_blank" >31-7 Packers beatdown of the Bears</a> that might as well have been by 100 points.</p><p>Maybe Mike Ditka saw it too. Imagine what the Bears coach who made Lambeau Field his personal playground would’ve thought about his old team’s no-show performance.</p><p>The Packers rubbed the Bears’ faces in the dirt. Their coach, Matt LaFleur, took Johnson’s lunch money, gave him a swirly and stuffed him in a locker. The better team out of these two? Please. The 3-2 records might be the same, but it isn’t even close.</p><p>Perhaps Johnson sensed it when he said at halftime to ESPN 1000 sideline reporter Jason McKie, “We gotta play f——ng better. We gotta be f——ng better.” Then again, the Bears trailed just 14-7 at the time and still had four second-half turnovers to commit and loads of long completions by the Packers to suffer through.</p><p>Who knew Packers quarterback Jordan Love (25 of 31 for 367 yards and two touchdowns) was better than Bart Starr, Brett Favre or Aaron Rodgers? Who knew receivers Christian Watson (six catches, 143 yards, two touchdowns) and Matthew Golden (six catches, 123 yards) put Don Hutson, Sterling Sharpe and Donald Driver to shame? Who knew safety Xavier McKinney (two interceptions) should have his name immortalized on the Lambeau facade instead of LeRoy Butler?</p><p>Or maybe they were all just lucky to be toying with the Bears on a miserable day for the visitors.</p><p>“That was a great display that we had out there,” Watson said, puffed with rivalry pride. “It definitely felt a little extra.”</p><p>“I’m not gonna say it wasn’t big for us,” McKinney said. “I’m not gonna say we didn’t have the intensity and the urgency this whole week knowing [whom] our opponent was going to be.”</p><p>Ditka lost his first game here as Bears coach, in 1983. After that, it went completely the other way, Ditka’s teams winning eight of nine while one Packers offense after another could barely score. Even his last team, in 1992, blew out the Packers 30-10 at Lambeau, raising the Bears’ record to 4-3.</p><p>“Let me tell you something here,” Ditka said that day. “If we keep improving like we are, we have a chance to make something happen.”</p><p>Yeah, well, no. Those Bears ended up 5-11 and Ditka got fired. But then the Packers won 12 of the next 13 games, and 20 of the next 23, head-to-head. At Lambeau, the Bears are a pathetic 9-25 since the Ditka era.</p><p>“Got to love the excitement around the rivalry and all that,” LaFleur said, his record against the Bears — 13-2 — looking mighty impressive.</p><p>And the beatdowns go on.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Packers hold a moment of silence for Mike Ditka at Lambeau Field before today’s game— <a href="https://t.co/DiItnliVxh">pic.twitter.com/DiItnliVxh</a></p>— Jason Lieser (@JasonLieser) <a href="https://x.com/JasonLieser/status/2109328562616496332?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3></h3><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>A Caleb Comeback? </b>Williams could return for the Bears’ next game, in Atlanta on Sunday — otherwise known as not a minute too soon.</p><p><b>Bagent or Keenum? </b>Somebody has to be QB2 on this team — and maybe even the starter against the Falcons. Bagent was bad enough to be knocked down a peg, but will he be?</p><p><b>Defense in Disarray: </b>The Bears have serious coverage issues, especially if they can’t rely on having more of a pass rush. Where have we heard this story before?</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-grades-packers-tyson-bagent-chicago-green-bay-lambeau-field-nfl" >Bears’ grades are in. How bad was it against the Packers?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/packers-lead-bears-14-7-at-halftime-at-lambeau-field-after-costly-tyson-bagent-interception" target="_blank" >Bears stumble throughout embarrassing 31-7 loss to Packers amid turnovers by Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-bench-qb-tyson-bagent-after-two-interceptions-vs-packers-then-case-keenum-throws-one-too" >Bears bench QB Tyson Bagent after two interceptions vs. Packers, then Case Keenum throws one, too</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-packers-zaire-franklin-luther-burden-quit-final-score-31-7-nfl" >Packers’ Zaire Franklin fires back at Bears’ Luther Burden — ‘He quit’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson runs out of answers, unable to ignite offense in 31-7 loss to Packers
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — For the first time since the very early days of his time coaching <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>, Ben Johnson looked like he was out of answers Sunday against the Packers.</p><p>Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent couldn’t get anything going, so Johnson tried Case Keenum in the fourth quarter. Nothing. The rushing attack never found a groove. No one stepped up as a go-to option in the passing game.</p><p>Play after play failed, and the Packers crushed the Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field. It was the most lopsided and embarrassing loss for Johnson since the Lions ran him out of the building in his second game last season.</p><p>“When you can’t get in a rhythm offensively, I’ve got to look at myself first,” Johnson said. “What do we have in? Did we prepare the right way? What [were] the play calls?”</p><p>Johnson credited new Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon for having his number all day and said, “We knew we were going to get their best shot, and we sure did,” but maintained frustration that his team undermined itself with errors.</p><p>It was the Bears’ first game since <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/1985-bears-championship-team-remembers-former-coach-mike-ditka-as-tip-of-the-spear" >the death of former coach Mike Ditka</a> on Friday, and players wore a No. 89 decal on their helmets in honor of the number he wore as a Bears tight end in the 1960s. The Packers held a moment of silence for Ditka before the game.</p><p>Johnson immersed himself in this rivalry with his “[Expletive] the Packers” rant last season and by exchanging snippy shots with coach Matt LaFleur, but there was none of that after this one. He and LaFleur met briefly afterward, and Johnson appeared to say, “Good job,” while shaking LaFleur’s hand with a grimace.</p><p>He must have believed his team was beyond something this ugly, even with a backup quarterback. This is the same coach who felt emboldened enough to set his sights on the 2013 Broncos’ scoring record and a trip to the Super Bowl.</p><p>Who could deny him after the Bears opened with 59 points against the Panthers? They’ve totaled 60 over four games since then, however, and they’d now need to average nearly 44 per game.</p><p>That’s overly ambitious even with the possibility of quarterback Caleb Williams returning Sunday against the Falcons.</p><p>A week earlier, when Bagent was mediocre against the Jets, No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai was the engine of the offense with 146 yards rushing and two touchdowns. He missed the Packers game with a toe injury, and no one else showed up to save the day as Bagent completed 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards and two interceptions for a 27.4 passer rating before Johnson benched him.</p><p>“Super disappointed, but really can't look any further than the mirror,” Bagent said. “It really, starting with me, just didn't go our way.”</p><p>There was a flicker late in the third quarter when Bagent hit Colston Loveland for a seven-yard pass on fourth-and-four with the Bears down 23-7, but he threw an interception the very next play. Gannon fooled Bagent by showing a Cover 0 defense (no safety deep) before the snap, then the Packers flipped to a Cover 2 and had safety Xavier McKinney in perfect position to beat Loveland to the ball for his second pick of the game.</p><p>Keenum was no better. He walked into a golden opportunity at the Packers’ 31-yard line and threw an interception in the end zone on fourth-and-goal. He also lost a fumble in the fourth and finished 11-for-19 passing for 108 yards and a 52.1 rating.</p><p>Johnson, unwilling to concede, kept swinging to the end and had Keenum throw deep on fourth-and-21 from his own 21-yard line with 1:10 remaining.</p><p>A week after running an NFL season-high 89 plays and racking up 492 yards in a punt-free win over the Jets, the Bears managed just 246 yards against the Packers — their lowest under Johnson — and went 4 for 14 on third down.</p><p>That reheated the debate about whether Johnson should’ve stuck with Keenum, who lit up the Eagles in the first game after Williams’ hamstring injury, and Johnson wouldn’t say who he’d start against the Falcons if Williams remains out.</p><p>The Bears need everything he brings: dual-threat playmaking, improvisational wizardry, electric energy.</p><p>Johnson has managed his absence short term, and it’s not the end of the world to sit 3-2 with him on the verge of coming back. But his playbook alone can’t carry them for the long run.</p><p>Williams progressed from throwing on the side last week to practicing partially Friday to working out at Lambeau Field on Sunday morning. He appears to be on track to step back into his spot at practice Wednesday, but when asked about him playing against the Falcons, Johnson said, “It’s going to be close.”</p><p>If there’s anything uncertain about his health, it’d be prudent to wait until ensuing Thursday against the Patriots. Two games in five days might not be ideal for Williams coming off that injury, and there’s an extended break after the Patriots game leading up to the Nov. 2 visit to the defending champion Seahawks.</p><p>But for whatever amount of time the Bears have to wait for Williams, it’s on Johnson to figure out a solution. His ability to adjust and pivot has been his hallmark as the Bears’ coach, and he ran out of moves Sunday.</p>

entries.title: Packers' Zaire Franklin fires back at Bears' Luther Burden — 'He quit'
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin heard what <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-grades-packers-tyson-bagent-chicago-green-bay-lambeau-field-nfl" target="_blank" >Bears</a> receiver Luther Burden said Monday about making his rival want to quit.</p><p>Sunday, he had the last laugh.</p><p>“We see all the little weird stuff they be doing in the media and all the different stuff they be saying,” Franklin, who was traded from the Colts to the Packers in March, told Packers reporters after their <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >31-7 win</a> at Lambeau Field. “You’ve got guys that have never really made a real play in this league talking about making somebody quit. That’s weird. We don’t do that.</p><p>“He quit today, by the day. He didn’t want to play any more.”</p><p>On Monday, Burden said that “we just want to beat [the Packers] real bad and make them quit.”</p><h3>Notes</h3><p>• One week after he was benched for fumbling, D’Andre Swift led the Bears with 43 rushing yards on nine carries and added four catches for 30. The Bears' run game struggled otherwise. Backup running back Roschon Johnson, receiver Kalif Raymond and Burden combined to run 10 times for six yards. Burden had four carries for two yards.</p><p>• Bears rookie kick returner Zavion Thomas’ 61-yard return in the fourth quarter was his longest of the season.</p><p>• The Bears’ lone touchdown drive went 9 minutes, 10 seconds. They held the ball for 9:16 at the end of the game last week. Entering Sunday, there had been only eight instances, league-wide, of a nine-plus-minute drive this season.</p>

entries.title: Bears' Cairo Santos bemoans kick 'that got away'
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Whether because of a plumbing issue or just old-fashioned rivalry shenanigans, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> didn’t have hot water in their locker-room showers after their <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-grades-packers-tyson-bagent-chicago-green-bay-lambeau-field-nfl" target="_blank" >31-7 blowout loss</a> to the Packers on Sunday.</p><p>Bears kicker Cairo Santos said he probably needed a cold shower, anyway, after he missed his only field goal of the game, a 43-yarder midway through the third quarter that would have cut the lead to 20-10. The Bears’ field goal operation was another thing that went wrong Sunday.</p><p>Santos missed the kick heading into the north end zone, whose wind drove both kickers crazy Sunday. Packers kicker Trey Smack missed two field goals and an extra point. The two field goal misses, of 43 and 47 yards, were into the north end zone in the fourth quarter. His missed extra point was heading south.</p><p>“Kicking toward the north end zone, it was brutal,” Santos said.</p><p>The notes Santos took before the game showed the swirling wind eventually tailed further right than left. When he tossed grass in the air, though, it tailed left. He trusted his pregame notes — and missed to the left. The Bears don’t play many noon games at Lambeau Field — and even fewer when the weather was 73 degrees at kickoff, the way it was Sunday. Still, Santos wasn’t making excuses. </p><p>“I needed to be my best,” he said. “Definitely one that got away.”</p>

entries.title: White Sox express hope amid sadness, but they know next season won't be the same
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — The visitors’ clubhouse at Progressive Field wasn’t filled with despair after the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox’</a> loss Saturday night.</p><p>There certainly was sadness after the team lost its third consecutive game and let the Guardians off the hook after they dropped the first two in the American League Division Series. But there were lots of hugs and handshakes and enough smiles to belie the feeling.</p><p>“More to come,” an optimistic Davis Martin was overheard saying.</p><p>Sean Burke took an undeserved loss in Game 5, allowing the only runs on a two-run homer by Jose Ramirez, who hit a pitch that was almost in the dirt. That didn’t stop Burke from going person to person in the clubhouse, thanking, consoling and congratulating teammates, whichever fit the moment.</p><p>“These are my brothers,” Burke said. “I’ve played on a lot of teams in my life; this is definitely my favorite team I’ve ever played on.”</p><p>Miguel Vargas, who led the Sox by far with a 1.129 OPS in the series, felt the same way, making the end of the season harder to swallow.</p><p>“We just love each other so much in this clubhouse,” he said. “It’s not going to be the same next year, for sure.”</p><p>Indeed it won’t. It never is. Though much of the Sox’ young core figures to return, there are few guarantees. Some highly respected veterans such as Erick Fedde and Randal Grichuk probably won’t be back, and some highly rated prospects such as Caleb Bonemer and Roch Cholowsky could join the team. It might be great, but it won’t be this.</p><p>“It was a pretty unique group,” Grant Taylor said. “The contributions we had to the clubhouse, even from guys that weren’t on the field, like [injured] Mike Vasil, everyday guys, just having a good time. We were friends, which is not what you get out of a clubhouse a lot of times.”</p><p>“This is so different than last year for us,” said Chase Meidroth, referring to the third of three consecutive seasons with more than 100 losses. “This is a family; this is a brotherhood. We wanted to win for each other. I didn’t love baseball like this last year.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/10/sean-burke-chicago-white-sox-chris-getz-will-venable-cleveland-guardians-mlb-postseason-playoffs-starting-pitching" >Sean Burke gives White Sox what they’ve been missing — and need more of</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/11/the-white-sox-offense-powered-their-rise-and-its-holes-hastened-their-demise-munetaka-murakami" >The White Sox’ offense powered their rise, and its holes hastened their demise</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/10/optimistic-white-sox-fans-fill-ramova-theatre-for-alds-winner-take-all-watch-party" >White Sox playoff run ends in a ‘bummer,’ but South Side fans cherish unexpected ride</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>That was evident in the clubhouse after the game. Though the Sox struck out 21 times, setting the MLB record for strikeouts in a nine-inning game — postseason or regular season — there was some positivity and a feeling of “We showed you” amid some teary eyes and raw emotions.</p><p>“We proved we’re a good team,” Burke said. “We believed throughout the season when people were doubting us and said this wasn’t sustainable or this was a fluke. More importantly, we proved to ourselves that we can do this.”</p><p>“Starting from last year in the second half, we all believed that we could be a winning playoff team,” Colson Montgomery said. “And we carried that mentality into this year.”</p><p>“We stuck together,” Vargas said. “The vibes in the clubhouse, everything was so awesome, sharing the time with the guys this year. We created a brotherhood here that is going to be forever. It’s a tough one, but it’s just the beginning for us.”</p><p>Those who expect to be back expect to be better.</p><p>“I’m still swinging at the high-velocity pitches and breaking balls down, and the chase is there,” Munetaka Murakami said through a translator. “So I’ve got to be better in all the mechanics and all the aspects of baseball.”</p><p>“Get better next year; we’ll be ready,” Meidroth said. “Being here [was a] good experience for next year, coming to camp and knowing what you need to do to get where we’re at today.”</p><p>“Obviously, not the result we hoped for in this series, but this core will be together for a little bit,” Burke said. “As sad as it is now that the season’s over, there’s so many bright spots to look forward to and such a good future to look forward to for the White Sox.”</p><p>Sox fans have heard that before, and it has led to anything but. Team history is littered with one-offs. In 126 seasons, the Sox have made consecutive postseason appearances once, in 2020-21, and the first season was shortened by the pandemic.</p><p>It sounds like these Sox expect to make it two.</p><p>“We’ll be back next year,” Meidroth said, “and this group will keep getting stronger.”</p><p>“We know we probably should’ve got the job done,” Montgomery said, “but you got to take away what we did this year. There’s a lot to be proud of.”</p>

entries.title: The White Sox' offense powered their rise, and its holes hastened their demise
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — Why should the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> ever pitch to Guardians legend Jose Ramirez?</p><p>It wasn’t a specific question before his fateful fourth-inning two-run homer off an ankle-high Sean Burke curveball in Cleveland’s Game 5 victory on Saturday. Intentionally walking Ramirez would’ve pushed leadoff man Steven Kwan into scoring position with no outs in a scoreless game.</p><p>Rather it’s an existential one, after Ramirez came alive to drive in seven runs over three-straight Guardians wins, more than the White Sox’ American League-best offense managed as a team over the same span. Among Sox leadership, Ramirez was described with a term too profane to print, but one that connoted fear and respect despite his injury-marred season.</p><p>But as manager Will Venable examined the matrix of every pitcher versus hitter matchup prepared for him by his staff, using the club’s internal research to assign an expected run value to each possible confrontation the Sox might face, the data informed that rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter could be referred to in the same terms.</p><p>“The matchup against DeLauter was way worse for us,” Venable said, referencing that research while discussing an RBI triple David Sandline allowed to Ramirez in Game 3. “Not even close. It was a way worse matchup for us, so we decided to pitch to Ramírez.”</p><p>Efforts to statistically prove the effect of lineup protection have been a mixed bag in baseball research, but after the White Sox were beaten by the Guardians’ best player, DeLauter’s enabling of it stretched beyond going 5-for-20 with two walks and no extra-base hits in the ALDS.</p><p>For all the offensive might the White Sox wielded this season, as they struck out an unfathomable 53 times over three games that sent them home for the winter, Miguel Vargas lacked a partner forcing similar decisions.</p><p>Vargas hit .308/.591/.538 in the ALDS. Whether the Guardians intended to walk the opposing team’s best player at Barry Bonds-like rates (nine free passes in 22 plate appearances) or the plate discipline that saw the All-Star third baseman draw 101 walks this season contributed to it, the White Sox’ inability to make Cleveland pay for Vargas living on the basepaths hung over the result.</p><p>Walks are a force multiplier when the White Sox offense is bashing home runs at the rate they did in the regular season, and irrelevant when they can’t put the ball in play, foreshadowed by the league’s fifth-highest strikeout rate during the season. As the Sox offense broke out in the first half, with Vargas, Munetaka Murakami and Colson Montgomery as the big three run producers, the latter two having the two lowest contact rates in the sport was just an aesthetic concern.</p><p>But as Montgomery set the all-time single-season strikeout record, Murakami weathered a deep late-season slump, the Sox striking out at an otherworldly 40.5% clip for the whole postseason felt forewarned. Their best Game 5 scoring chance ended with their All-Star first baseman swinging through 95 mph down the pipe, and progressing farther in future years with this current dearth of contact skill is unlikely.</p><p>“It was less about chase and more about being attacked in the zone and swing and miss in the zone,” Venable said of his offense’s last effort. “Just didn't have what it would have taken to move some balls forward there, and I think obviously the story [was] just being able to put the ball in play.”</p><p>Struggles included, Murakami posted a .825 OPS and was a productive hitter in his first exposure to major league pitching, showed up in great physical shape and saved his best defense for the postseason. But where extending his two-year contract once seemed imperative, it now must be balanced against the long-term challenges of maintaining a swing that can produce a preponderance of whiffs when his hands drift out of their ideal path for a week.</p><p>Similarly entering the 2027 season with plenty to prove will be Montgomery. The power to pop 31 homers in a season in which he was often out of sync is rarely combined with palatable shortstop defense. For all their shortstop-heavy drafts, the Sox are a year and/or a healthy William Bergolla Jr. away from any in-house challengers at Montgomery’s position.</p><p>But Montgomery’s approach and swing path wavered in the second half and he slid to the bottom of the lineup for a reason. And even though Murakami authored the biggest Sox swing of the series in Game 1, walking Vargas to attack him was a winning strategy for the Guardians.</p><p>“We're still a very young team,” Murakami said via interpreter after Game 5, while also lamenting his midseason injury. “We need to, we have to learn from our experience here and then bring that to next year.”</p><p>The White Sox think Braden Montgomery will provide much more when his swing gets efficient enough to elevate the ball consistently, Kyle Teel only showed flashes of his 2025 form amid injuries, and top prospect Caleb Bonemer’s eventual arrival should lessen the reliance on veteran right-handed platoon bats.</p><p>But the White Sox offense didn’t flounder in the ALDS because it simply wasn’t their time yet. Holes were exploited, and opponents will be probing for more. They can get better, but the road will also only get tougher.</p><p>“People are going to be gunning for our heads next year,” hitting coach Derek Shomon told the Sun-Times. “Rightfully so, they should be. So, you act accordingly.”</p>
